## Nobara's room and Maki's

2 rows, each painted twice: the two friends' rooms off the girls' corridor. Nobody is in either picture, and nothing in them carries lettering.

Run this in the **local ComfyUI**. Press **Run** once.

Each row is one picture, painted twice: **version A** on top, **version B** under it. You choose between them afterwards.

The **Load Image** boxes on the left should already show their pictures. If one shows an error, click **choose file to upload** and pick the file with the same name from `JJK Game images/ui2/early`.

**Cost:** 4 pictures, about **$0.64** (Nano Banana Pro, about $0.16 a picture, charged to your Comfy account).

You don't need to save anything: the results go to ComfyUI's output folder and Claude picks them up from there.

If it stops with a rate-limit or "high demand" error, wait a minute and press **Run** again: a finished picture is reused, not paid for twice (as long as ComfyUI hasn't been restarted).

widgets_values: This is a background picture for a visual novel: a new picture of one room of a traditional Japanese mountain school, built of timber and white plaster. Picture 1 is the house this room is in, cut from a picture already painted and seen from outside: two storeys of white plaster and timber, with latticed windows and flower boxes. Picture 2 is the upstairs corridor of the same house, already painted: the new room has the same pale plaster, brown timber, timber floor and the same kind of door. Picture 3 is the garden this house stands on, already painted: what is seen through the new room's window is that garden from upstairs in the house on its right. Do not copy the camera or the layout of any of the three: the new picture is taken indoors, in a bedroom. THE PLACE: a bedroom upstairs in the girls' dormitory, the house of white plaster and timber of picture 1: neat and well dressed, about five metres long and four wide. I stand inside at one end and look along the room. In the left wall, near me, is the door, a brown timber door like those of picture 2, shut. Beyond the door, along the left wall, stands a bed, neatly made with a bright quilt and nothing lying on it, and a small bedside lamp, switched off, on a low table at its head. Against the far wall, right of the middle, stands a tall dressing mirror in a timber frame, its glass showing only the room; beside it stands a desk with a canvas roll of tools, rolled up and tied, lying on it. On the floor along the far wall stands a neat row of paper shopping bags in plain colours, with nothing printed on them. In the right wall, further along than the middle, is a wide window with a slim timber lattice, like the windows of picture 1: through it I see flowers in the window box just outside, the garden's pond below, the two-storey house of dark timber with its upstairs gallery across the garden, and to one side of it the low house with glass doors on its deck. The stretch of the right wall nearest me is plain plaster. The floor is timber boards, clear and open across the whole bottom of the picture. No lettering and no maker's mark anywhere in the picture: none on any bag, box, book or wall. The picture is seen from standing eye height, the horizon a little above the middle. The right ninth of the picture and its top-left corner hold nothing one would walk to or use: there the walls are plain plaster and timber, painted fully, to the picture's very edge. THE LOOK: a real place you could walk into, drawn as a clean modern anime background. Believable materials (wood grain, glass with soft reflections, stone, plaster, fabric), physically believable light with soft shadows and bounced light, real depth. Clean and well kept: walls are fresh and even, with no stains, cracks, peeling, damp patches or dirt, and there is no dust, litter or fallen leaves on the floor or the ground; everything that belongs to the place is still there. Crisp precise edges, clean clear colour, no film grain, no noise, no canvas texture, no visible brush strokes, no haze or glow washing out detail. Through every window a clear, in-focus view. No people, no animals, no text, no logos. Output a 16:9 picture.
